clue.text: Old statesman and Commander-in-Chief meeting Cockney super-guy

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for Commander-in-Chief
a super-guy is a hero, and a Cockney drops the opening H

explanation.surface: A Roman politician and a military chief meet an East End superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (working-class Londoners) traditionally drop their aitches, so a hero becomes 'ero.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the celebrated orator and politician of the late Roman Republic, an ancient statesman.

clue.text: One doing the rounds with many clubs?

definitions.text: One doing the rounds with many clubs?

blocks.clueFragment: One doing the rounds with many clubs?
blocks.note: surface reading: a socialite visiting many nightclubs in turn

blocks.clueFragment: doing the rounds with many clubs
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone accompanying a golfer round the course carrying a bag of golf clubs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' and 'clubs' suggest a night out; on a golf course a round is a game and clubs are what you hit the ball with.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's bag and clubs during each round of golf.

clue.text: Shift in opinion could do for Earth

blocks.note: first meaning: a reversal of one's view or feelings
second, cryptic meaning: rearranging the letters of the word heart would produce the word earth

explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes the answer's own wordplay: shuffle the letters of the last word of the answer and you get Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A change of heart is an idiom for altering one's mind or attitude about something.

clue.text: End wearing torn garment

indicators.note: something wearing a coat has it around it, so the second word wraps the first

blocks.note: rent is an old past tense of rend, to tear
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A tip of fabric sticking through a ripped piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for clothing, so it names a garment or attire.

clue.text: Little devil in the manner of a beast

blocks.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
the borrowed French phrase à la means in the style of

explanation.surface: A small demon behaves like a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, so it is one kind of beast or wild animal.

clue.text: Maiden said to be ethical

blocks.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A young woman is reported to be principled.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, marked M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral and ethical are synonyms, both meaning concerned with right and wrong behaviour.

clue.text: Significant dates that could make insane sir rave

indicators.note: could make suggests something formed out of raw material, so the letters are reworked into a new word

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Important days might drive a knight to rant like a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Anniversaries are the yearly returns of important occasions, dates marked as meaningful.

clue.text: A group of directors on a ship?

blocks.note: taken as written
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: A company's executives are on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a playful reading: the board of directors sitting on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or onto a ship, plane or train, carried as a passenger.

clue.text: A desire troubled beloved people

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and stirred up, so the letters are put out of their order

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A longing that has been disturbed affects those one loves.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearies is an affectionate term for people one is fond of, the plural of dearie, a darling.

clue.text: Europeans in resort with terrible drains

indicators.note: terrible things are in a dreadful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: a spa is a health resort
the letters of drains, rearranged

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers from the continent stuck in a town with awful plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaniards are the people of Spain, a European nation, so they are a kind of European.

clue.text: Music from some traveller on doorstep

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A wandering musician plays a tune at someone's front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Unmarried person abandoning spot of sun in warm spot

indicators.note: a spot of something is just a tiny bit of it, here only its opening letter
abandoning means leaving something behind, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a single is someone not married
the first letter of the word sun

explanation.surface: A bachelor leaves the sunshine for somewhere warm.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE loses its S to leave INGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fireplace or hearth, as in inglenook, so it is literally a warm place in the house.

clue.text: A large sweetheart completely done with

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large on clothing labels
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A big romance is entirely finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is all over has ended entirely, finished and done with.

clue.text: Trader dismissed — needing to get healthier?

blocks.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
fitter means in better health

explanation.surface: A merchant who has been sacked needs to improve his health.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shopkeeper who sells clothing and equipment, a kind of retailer.

clue.text: Giant, one bearing down on a queen

blocks.note: a titan is a giant
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge person and a companion press down on a female monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'bearing down on' places the first pieces on top of the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Wood and mineral on the beach?

blocks.note: ash is a kind of tree and its timber
ore is rock from which minerals are mined

explanation.surface: Driftwood and pebbles found lying at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land, on or towards the shore from the water.

clue.text: Shelf with right sort of book

blocks.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bookshelf holding the proper kind of volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is an account book in which financial transactions are recorded.

clue.text: Student of the sun, companion welcomed in

indicators.note: welcomed in means taken inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: solar means of the sun
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A student of the sun brings in a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the sun' looks like part of what the student studies; 'Student' alone is the definition and 'the sun' is solar.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or a student, especially one holding a scholarship.

clue.text: Falsehood associated with good English lord once

blocks.note: a lie is a falsehood
G is the abbreviation for good
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A dishonest statement linked to a decent English aristocrat of old.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a liege was the superior to whom vassals owed allegiance, a historic overlord.

clue.text: Traffic to hurry round far side of village

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read back to front
the far side of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: to dart is to move quickly
the last letter of village

explanation.surface: Vehicles rushing round the edge of a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' reads as cars, but it is the noun meaning commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in its older sense is buying and selling, as in drug traffic, which is commerce or trade.

clue.text: Leaders of old regime had to speak in public?

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters, so only the first of each is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words
to have a meal is to eat, so had can mean ate

explanation.surface: Former dictators were obliged to address the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal speech, a pompous way of saying address an audience.

clue.text: Some ladies in gingham, doing a number

indicators.note: some means only a part of the following words, a run of letters lying inside them

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word to the middle of the third

explanation.surface: Women in checked cotton dresses perform a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Gingham is a checked cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece in a performance, so doing one means performing a song.

clue.text: Girl presenting French art to the King

blocks.note: in French tu es means thou art
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A young woman shows some French artwork to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is not painting but the old second-person form of be, as in thou art.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a female first name, and crosswords use girl to signal any woman's name.

clue.text: Roman ruler put off by a scare

indicators.note: put off suggests being thrown out of its proper state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An emperor is deterred by a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of Roman emperors, after Julius Caesar, so it names a ruler of Rome.
